prompt:
Pixel-art sprite sheet, single image, fully transparent background.

SUBJECT: the undead zombie basketball player in the attached reference image.
Match that character exactly: sickly grey-green skin, ragged mid-brown hair,
sunken eyes with small pale pupils, a lipless grin showing the teeth, dark
rotted patches on the arms and legs, a torn and ragged blue sleeveless
basketball jersey with a yellow number 13, torn blue shorts with white and
yellow trim, white high-top sneakers with blue and yellow flashes over white
socks. Identical colours, identical proportions, identical build and identical
height as the reference, in every frame.

LAYOUT: one horizontal row of 3 frames of equal width, evenly spaced. No
borders, no frame numbers, no labels, no background, no drop shadows.

POSE GUIDE: TWO images are attached, and they do different jobs.

The COLOUR image of the character is the only authority on WHO HE IS. His
colours, his proportions, his build, his height, his face, his kit and the
drawing style all come from that image and from the SUBJECT above, and nothing
below changes any of them. It does NOT decide which way he faces: the FRAMES
below do.

The other image is a POSE GUIDE: a stick figure on a white background, standing
in a row on one ground line, in the same left-to-right order as the FRAMES
listed below. The Nth figure in the pose guide is the pose for the Nth frame.
Take the GEOMETRY from it and only the geometry: where each foot stands on the
ground line, how deeply the knees are bent, how low the shoulders and head are,
and where the elbows and hands are. Where the words below and the pose guide
describe the same thing, they agree; the pose guide is the exact version of it.

THE COLOURS ON THE POSE GUIDE name the limbs: the RED arm and the ORANGE leg
are on the VIEWER'S RIGHT, the BLUE arm and the GREEN leg on the viewer's left.

THE HEAD ON THE POSE GUIDE: in the first figure the upright line and the level
line mark the centre of his face, looking at the viewer. A head with a small
TRIANGLE jutting out of one side is seen in profile: the triangle is his nose,
pointing the way he looks. A head with THREE CURVED STROKES across it and an
oval on each side has NO face: we are looking at the BACK of his head, the
strokes are the hair on the back of his skull, the ovals his two ears.

SEEN FROM BEHIND, his hands are in FRONT of his body, so where the pose guide
puts them in front of his chest they are hidden from the viewer by his own
back: only the elbows, sticking out to either side, show that his arms are bent
and raised.

Draw the character from the colour reference standing in those positions. The
pose guide is an instruction, not artwork: its thin lines, its colours, its
joint dots, its white background, its circular head, its triangle, its ovals
and its strokes are NOT part of the drawing and must not appear anywhere in it.

CAMERA: locked off. Identical distance and eye level in every frame. The
character must be exactly the same height in every frame, and the same height
as in the reference image — do not zoom, crop, recompose or rescale between
frames. All frames share one ground line: the soles of the feet touch the same
horizontal line in every frame.

VIEW: back view, seen from directly behind, squared away from the viewer and
looking up toward a basket high in front of him.

FRAMES, left to right:
1. CALIBRATION POSE: standing straight upright, feet shoulder-width apart, arms
   hanging relaxed at his sides, facing the viewer, in the plain neutral
   standing pose from the reference image. This exact pose appears as the first
   frame of every sheet in this set and must be drawn identically every time.
2. Knees slightly bent, feet shoulder-width apart, both hands raised in front
   of the chest as if cradling something -- out of sight behind his back, only
   the bent elbows showing at his sides -- head tilted up.
3. The same pose settled very slightly lower: knees a touch more bent, hands a
   fraction lower, weight eased. A small breathing settle, nothing more -- the
   two frames should be close.

This row is a seamless loop: frame 3 must flow back into frame 2 with no jump.

STYLE: VGA-era 256-colour DOS-game pixel art, drawn pixel by pixel — NOT a
modern illustration with a pixel filter over it. The limits below are the look;
keep all of them: - At most THREE tones per material: a base, one darker
shadow, one lighter highlight. Hard edges between the tones. - NO gradients, NO
soft or airbrushed shading, NO glow, NO bloom, and NO anti-aliasing anywhere —
not on the outline, not between tones, not around the silhouette. - Where a
tone change needs softening, use visible ORDERED DITHER — a checkerboard of the
two tones. Dither, never blend. - Chunky square pixels on one consistent grid,
plainly visible at full size. - A bold dark outline around the silhouette and
around the major forms inside it. The background must be fully transparent
(alpha 0) with no haze, glow or soft fringe around the silhouette. Output a
wide landscape image.

The character is NOT holding a basketball in any frame — the ball is drawn
separately by the game.
